Jasmine — looping in Marissa as lead on IP indemnity. Quick read: Acme is pushing hard on defend for model output; that's our largest exposure. I propose a three-part compromise we can push back with: 

1) Scope narrowing: Indemnity applies only to third-party claims asserting infringement from model outputs generated using Redwood-hosted models (exclude customer fine-tuning artifacts and customer-supplied data).
2) Notice & cooperation: Maintain 30-day notice but require customer to provide the evidence matrix (see attached) within 10 business days of notice; default cooperation obligations otherwise.
3) Remedies & offsets: Keep overall cap at contracted amounts but carve out defense costs up to a $3M escrow for material deals; require carrier/insurance offset language.

I'll draft suggested redline language and a short cover memo. If Sales wants defend for larger deals, we should tie that to a premium and escrow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attached are marked redlines and a short playbook of stakeholder asks — this is focused on evidence handoff, customer obligations, and a tiered defense-control ladder. Key points in the redline: 
- Add explicit exclusion for customer-modified models and downstream derivative claims.
- Define evidence kit (what we need within 10 business days): original prompt data, timestamps, model config, sample outputs.
- If customer fails to provide kit, defense obligations reduce to reimburse-only.

I also added a fallback that allows Redwood to pursue settlement approval rights and implement technical mitigations (model updates, rate limiting) pending dispute resolution.

Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Jasmine — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines from your counsel. A few clarifying questions from Acme Legal: 
1) The evidence kit timeline (10 business days) may be tight for cross-functional collection — can we agree on 15 business days for a global customer?
2) If Redwood pursues technical mitigations, what is the SLA to notify Acme and avoid disruption? We need a 5-7 business day notice before rate limiting or limits are applied that materially affect production.
3) On the escrow: Acme prefers an insurance-first approach; can Redwood agree to seek defense coverage from carriers before drawing on escrow?

Happy to take these on a quick call tomorrow.

Best,

Dave/Marta — thanks for the questions; quick response and next steps below so we can lock for Thursday's commercial review: 

1) Evidence kit timing: Redwood can accept 15 business days for global customers, provided Acme includes an initial acknowledgement and commencement of evidence collection within 5 business days of notice. If the kit is incomplete after 15 days, we revert to reimburse-only.

2) Technical mitigations & SLA: Redwood will provide a 7-business-day notice for rate limiting or production-impacting mitigations and publish a short incident playbook for mitigation steps. Connor will own the playbook deliverable (see related Drive link).

3) Escrow vs insurance: Redwood agrees to seek coverage from primary carriers before tapping escrow; escrow is a last resort during indemnity draw. We will add an insurance-first clause and require Coop to present carrier declination before escrow access.

Next steps: Kimberly/Marissa to produce final redline with the language above by end of day Wednesday; Ben to prepare the two commercial options for Thursday (12% uplift vs $50k escrow + pilot). I'll schedule the call and include the DocuSign link for a short form amendment if we land on the defend option.

Thanks all — see attachments for the current redline and the evidence playbook.
